paths.description: Entry page and content-discovery hub; covers global navigation, hero, rankings, performance, privacy, and responsive behavior.
Novel discovery/search archetype; covers taxonomy navigation and mobile browsing.
Representative work-detail archetype; covers metadata, calls to read, episode list, and images.
Primary reading journey and long-form reader archetype; covers prose, reader chrome, no-JS content, and long-page behavior.
Anonymous login/signup entry; covers authentication options and passkey availability without creating an account.
Deliberate invalid route; covers HTTP failure messaging and recovery.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Dark-emulated screenshots of both the home and reading surfaces remain white, and computed color-scheme is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, border, and control tokens.

findings.summary: High-contrast preferences are not comprehensively supported.
findings.evidence: The prefers-contrast screenshot is effectively unchanged, while Lighthouse reports color-contrast failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Add prefers-contrast and forced-colors treatments, and fix baseline WCAG contrast failures.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not expose declarative view transitions.
findings.evidence: The CSS/runtime probe found no view-transition rules, while the representative journey spans listing, work, and episode pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive-enhancement View Transitions for route and reader state changes, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long reading and listing pages provide no scroll-state-aware progress cue.
findings.evidence: The episode is over 10,000 CSS px high, but CSS inspection found no scroll timeline or scroll-state rules and the reader screenshot has no progress indicator.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight declarative reading-progress indicator or scroll-state-aware reader chrome.

findings.summary: Core public templates render desktop-width layouts on mobile.
findings.evidence: At 360 px, layout captures report 825 px overflow on home and explore, 640 px on work, and 380 px on the episode. Screenshots show clipped headings, navigation, controls, and content.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace fixed minimum widths with intrinsic responsive layouts; keep every template within the visual viewport.

findings.summary: Components do not adapt at their reuse boundary.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no container queries and multiple templates retain wide desktop component geometry at 360 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Define containment for reusable cards, grids, and reader chrome, then adapt them with size container queries.

findings.summary: Some controls have inaccessible names or undersized touch targets.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails target-size and link-name audits; the carousel button probe shows two icon-only buttons without aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Give icon controls accessible names, provide at least 44 by 44 CSS px targets with spacing, and retain visible focus styles.

findings.summary: Mobile load responsiveness misses the performance baseline.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports LCP 3.1 s, TBT 740 ms, interactive at 24.9 s, and a performance score of 0.72.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, reduce startup JavaScript, and schedule non-critical work after the core content is usable.

findings.summary: Long JavaScript tasks block the main thread.
findings.evidence: The trace records two long tasks up to 140 ms and 177 ms TBT; Lighthouse under throttling reports 740 ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks, defer analytics and advertising work, and use task priorities for non-user-blocking work.

findings.summary: The critical delivery path is fragmented and cache hygiene is weak.
findings.evidence: HAR records 139 requests, seven parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets, and major images without cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, confirm script defer semantics, and set durable immutable caching on versioned assets.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JavaScript and third-party code.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 519 KiB unused JavaScript; HAR attributes 1.30 MB and 85 requests to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate tags, load analytics and ad code conditionally, and split non-critical application code.

findings.summary: Several images, frames, and links lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails image-alt, frame-title, link-name, and label-content-name-mismatch; its accessibility score is 0.72.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide meaningful alt text, title embedded frames, and ensure every focusable link/control has a matching accessible name.

findings.summary: Text does not consistently meet WCAG contrast minimums.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse’s axe-backed color-contrast audit fails on the home page.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA in normal and high-contrast conditions.

findings.summary: The home page lacks a main landmark and has weak control semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails landmark-one-main and link-name; DOM probing found zero main and zero nav elements, and only a 1 px dotted focus outline on the first link.
findings.suggestedFix: Use main/nav landmarks, repair names, and provide a clearly visible focus-visible indicator in logical reading order.

findings.summary: Mobile clipping makes text difficult or impossible to read.
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots clip long headings, tabs, metadata, and reader content because templates are 740 to 1,185 px wide.
findings.suggestedFix: Reflow prose and headings within the viewport using fluid measure, wrapping, and responsive typography.

findings.summary: The viewport explicitly disables user zoom.
findings.evidence: Every inspected public page declares maximum-scale=1.0 and user-scalable=no; Lighthouse fails meta-viewport and target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable restrictions, then verify 200% and 400% reflow and target spacing.

findings.summary: Production load emits browser and React errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse records a CORS failure, net::ERR_FAILED, and React hydration error #418 in the console.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix the hydration mismatch and third-party CORS integration; prevent expected network failures from surfacing as application errors.

findings.summary: Image markup does not reserve dimensions consistently.
findings.evidence: The work-page image audit finds 27 of 31 images without width/height and 11 oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio and request image widths close to rendered sizes.

findings.summary: The page has deprecations, BFCache blockers, and missing source maps.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports one deprecated API, three BFCache failure reasons, missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript, and inspector issues.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API use and unload-style BFCache blockers, and publish correct production source maps.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The home metadata probe finds no canonical URL and /sitemap.xml returns 404, although robots permits crawling.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish canonical links on indexable templates and a sitemap referenced from robots.txt.

findings.summary: Content pages provide social metadata but no structured entity data.
findings.evidence: The work page has Open Graph metadata but no JSON-LD, and the home probe also finds no structured-data scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Add schema.org JSON-LD for WebSite and CreativeWork/Book-style entities that matches visible content.

findings.summary: Transport policy and cookie attributes are unsafe by default.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP and HSTS are absent; 9 of 9 observed cookies are flagged insecure and several use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing CSP and HSTS, then mark all HTTPS cookies Secure and use the narrowest SameSite policy.

findings.summary: The anonymous home page has a large tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe sees 35 third-party origins and 14 known trackers; HAR records 85 third-party requests and 1.30 MB transferred.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendors, gate non-essential tracking on consent, minimise event payloads, and batch necessary analytics.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defenses are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers lack CSP, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy, while clickjacking and nosniff protections are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add strict Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy alongside CSP/HSTS; consider Trusted Types for the React surface.

findings.summary: Runtime layout is not robust at narrow viewport edges.
findings.evidence: Menus and content extend hundreds of pixels beyond the mobile viewport on four public templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Use intrinsic responsive layout and edge-aware overlay positioning so content and controls remain reachable.

findings.summary: Several assets are oversized or lack efficient delivery metadata.
findings.evidence: The image audit flags 11 oversized work-page images; HAR’s largest image is 483 KB and major images lack cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve resolution-appropriate modern images, preserve responsive sources, and cache immutable assets.

findings.summary: Background advertising and analytics create disproportionate work.
findings.evidence: HAR logs 34 fetch/XHR requests, many ad-auction and conversion calls, and 85 third-party requests on an anonymous landing page.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritise and conditionally load background fetches, consolidate analytics, and remove redundant vendors.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts dominate the page budget.
findings.evidence: Of 3.24 MB transferred, 1.30 MB is third-party; Google Tag Manager and Facebook alone transfer about 924 KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget and delay non-essential vendors until user intent or consent.

findings.summary: The initial memory footprint is heavy for a content landing page.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contains 869,025 nodes and 48.4 MB self size before extended interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile constructor and DOM populations, remove duplicate vendor runtimes, and lazy-create below-fold components.
